title: D1a Identity Directory And Legacy Data Fence
summary: Dev56/schema024 restricts the directory to actual-owner personal spaces. Foreign memberships grant nothing and member mutation is disabled. Account CAS, audit and RLS remain; login and complete content isolation are not implemented.

migration.policy: Explicit policy-only migration. Migrations001..023 and historical records remain unchanged. No inferred ownership, upload or source export.
migration.rollback: Restore a matched previous binary/configuration/data set separately. Old binaries reject schema024. No live down-migration or history deletion.

externalIdentityIncrement.behavior: Explicit immutable issuer/subject binding, own metadata reads, maintenance account inventory and binding-state CAS/audit; native resolution observes current account/binding state and never grants admin or static project permissions.
externalIdentityIncrement.boundary: Historical dev69 boundary. Dev71 wires optional OIDC session admission and dynamic personal workers; native login and management UI remain pending. Migration infers no external identity or owner.

admission.identity: Authenticated configured principal, never caller-supplied account/tenant headers.
admission.enrollment: Explicit legacy maintenance admin operation for an existing non-admin principal. Enrollment never assigns old projects or workspaces.
admission.legacy: Unenrolled principals retain prior project grants only while none intersects an explicitly bound project; schema021 adds the fence described in shin-workspace-ownership-v1.json. Registered accounts cannot use any legacy data route, including telemetry, source, Observer ingestion, checkpoints, retrieval, receipts and publication; HTTP403 identity-data-plane-not-enabled. Health/live remains process-only.
admission.disabled: Next authenticated HTTP request observes disabled account and returns401 account-disabled, including readiness. Already in-flight reads may finish. Identity mutation authorization is rechecked inside its serialized transaction.
admission.maintenance: Existing static admin remains trusted legacy maintenance authority, not a normal user/operator role. It cannot be enrolled via HTTP. Do not expose this listener publicly.

routes.access: Actual active owner's personal spaces; explicit maintenance overview
routes.query: after identifier, limit1..100 default20, next_cursor or null

routes.access: Actual active owner or explicit maintenance; otherwise404
Disabled for all callers:403 sharing-disabled; no mutation or audit

consistency.creation: Exact natural-key retry returns current resource and replayed=true; conflicting attributes return409. This is not replay of a frozen historical response.
consistency.membership: Only initial owner membership is created with the personal space. Historical memberships remain stored but cannot authorize cross-user access. No invitation, membership-edit, ownership-transfer or deletion API.
consistency.audit: Each committed mutation appends metadata-only audit in the same transaction. Failed CAS, denied writes and creation retries append nothing. Audit insert failure rolls back mutation.
consistency.locking: One advisory transaction lock serializes low-volume directory writes; existing database statement/lock deadlines apply. Not yet a hundreds-of-users throughput qualification.
consistency.bounds: Identifiers use existing identifier grammar, display names1..120bytes, revision nonnegative below INT64_MAX, list at most100. Existing HTTP body/queue/pool bounds apply. Lifetime directory quotas and audit retention remain before production onboarding.

isolation.database: The four directory tables use ENABLE/FORCE RLS. Runtime is non-owner, non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS. Every directory transaction resets authorization GUCs (five in schema020, six with schema021 ownership); pool leases cannot retain another request's scope.
isolation.drift: Readiness checks exact columns, RLS flags, schema-owner table ownership, eight policy shapes and key constraints. Unknown deparsed policy shape fails closed and requires PostgreSQL-version qualification.
isolation.threatBoundary: RLS defends application scope mistakes, not a malicious process with the runtime DB password, same-UID attacker, database owner or superuser. GUCs are trusted server-side context, not an independent credential.
isolation.content: All tenant responses state content_access=not-enabled. Existing data tables, caches, jobs and vectors are not tenant-isolated by this migration. D1b is mandatory.
